issues.issue: Floating representation does not itself constrain values to0–1; normalization must be explicit.

Displayed NumPy crop has an empty width for the shown shape; both crop orders are reversed for the intended rectangle under the current Image u,v API. Image index order changed in version1.0; source version is unspecified.
Displayed coordinate-domain H/W order is inconsistent with horizontal u and vertical v.
A dark histogram does not alone establish underexposure; separate RGB marginals lose joint color pairing.
Modulo arithmetic depends on the retained dtype; float images are not inherently normalized. Current Image.to("float") means float32, not the printed float64 comment.
Brightness addition has intensity units, not spatial pixels; threshold Boolean storage differs from0/255 display. Prose and marker coordinates differ, so questions do not silently reconcile them.
Input118/min91/max138 imply146.4893617, not output235; marker axes and label appear exchanged. The displayed gamma power gives0.78814093 at118.
Discrete histogram equalization need not yield a uniform histogram and may enhance noise.
The top Gaussian exponent omits factor2, inconsistent with the worked standard formula. Finite sampled normalization and binomial approximation are distinguished.
Convolution/correlation equality needs180-degree rotational symmetry, not merely transpose symmetry; finite Fourier boundary conventions remain explicit.
Reflection padding conventions differ, and no boundary rule universally gives the smoothest or most physically correct result.
Not every linear filter is an averaging filter; signed derivative filters are counterexamples.
Median output is not guaranteed noise-free and can remove fine structures.
Linear smoothing does not fail universally; correlation scores and gradients require task-specific interpretation.
